samples.summary: Untrusted `dp` is clamped only at render time; nothing validates it at the write/ingest boundary, so an `.xlsx` import can persist an arbitrarily large `dp` into the shared document
samples.evidence: The delta's own rationale (format.ts:17-21) names "an imported `.xlsx`, a collaborator's document" as the threat model, and fixes the crash by clamping inside `formatValue` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/format.ts:182). But the producing side is unbounded: `decimalPlaces()` (xlsx-styles.ts:178-181) returns `match[1].length` for a `formatCode` like `0.` followed by N zeros, and that value is written straight into the style at xlsx-styles.ts:413 (`if (numberFormat.dp !== undefined) style.dp = numberFormat.dp;`). An attacker who gets a victim to import a crafted workbook (or a collaborator with write access) therefore stores e.g. `dp: 30000` on many cells: it now renders harmlessly, but the garbage value is persisted and replicated to every collaborator, inflates the CRDT document against the per-document size cap, and any future consumer of `style.dp` that does not route through `clampDecimals` re-opens the RangeError/DoS this change closed. Defense in depth wants a clamp where the value enters the model, not only where it is painted. I grepped every `style.dp` producer/consumer to confirm no other write-side clamp exists.

samples.summary: `changeDecimals` steps an untrusted stored `dp` and writes the result back unsanitized: a non-finite stored `dp` yields `{dp: NaN}` persisted into the shared document
samples.evidence: `getActiveDecimalState()` returns `style.dp` verbatim (sheet.ts:4183-4184) with no validation. In `changeDecimals`, `const stepped = Math.min(dp + delta, MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES)` (sheet.ts:4202) only bounds the upper end. If a hostile document/import stored `dp: NaN` (or a non-numeric value that coerces to NaN — `dp` is typed `number` but nothing validates remote/imported style objects), then `NaN + delta = NaN`, `Math.min(NaN, 20) = NaN`, `NaN < 0` is false, so `clamped` is false and `target` is `NaN`; sheet.ts:4236 then writes `{ dp: NaN }` through `setRangeStyle` into the CRDT/JSON document. `clampDecimals` is applied only on the render side (format.ts:182), never before the write, so the victim's own client is what launders the bad value into persisted state (and NaN has no well-defined JSON/CRDT encoding — `JSON.stringify` turns it into `null`, and equality-based logic such as `unsetRangeStyleValues({dp, nf})` can never match a NaN, so the round-trip guarantees silently stop holding). Marginal impact is limited because the attacker needed write access to plant the original `dp`, hence minor. Fix: run the stepped value through `clampDecimals` before it is written.

samples.summary: Decrease-decimals now does per-cell effective-style resolution plus two Intl formats over every populated cell of the selection — a hostile/large shared document turns one keypress into an unbounded main-thread stall
samples.evidence: `selectionRendersAt` previously did a cheap string scan per cell; this delta adds `parseRef(sref)` + `this.resolveEffectiveStyle(ref.r, ref.c, cell.s)` per cell (sheet.ts:4261-4263), and `resolveEffectiveStyle` calls `resolveRangeStyleAt(this.rangeStyles, row, col)` (sheet.ts:887), which scans the stored range-style patches, then allocates a merged object. `unsetKeepsRendering` does the same plus two `formatValue` calls per cell (sheet.ts:4302-4310), each of which builds a fresh Intl formatter via `toLocaleString` (no formatter cache in format.ts:40-60). With Select-All, `selectionTargets()` covers the whole used range, so the work is O(populated cells x range-style patches) synchronously inside one UI action. A collaborator who fills a shared document with many styled cells and many range-style patches can make a single Decrease-decimal-places press freeze the victim's tab. Self-triggered and only a liveness issue, so minor; I did not measure an actual hang, hence low confidence.

samples.summary: The new fail-open formatting chain silently drops the currency style for an attacker-supplied `cu`, so a currency cell renders as a bare number with no indication of failure
samples.evidence: `cu` reaches `formatValue` straight from stored style (gridcanvas.ts:1596-1598, sheet.ts:972-974) and is never validated as a well-formed ISO 4217 code (input.ts:335 takes it from a `slice`, and no schema validates remote style). With a malformed `cu`, both the locale attempt (format.ts:46) and the options attempt (format.ts:51) throw, so the third fallback `value.toLocaleString('en-US')` (format.ts:56) returns e.g. `1.5` — the currency marker is dropped entirely and nothing is logged or surfaced. The added test only asserts `.toContain('1.5')`, i.e. it encodes this behaviour. Trading a crash for silence is the right direction, but for financial data the fail-open outcome is a display-integrity/spoofing vector: a collaborator (or a crafted import) can make monetary cells read as plain unmarked numbers for every other viewer, on every render. Preferable: validate/normalize `cu` (3 alpha chars, else fall back to the locale currency) so the currency style survives the failure.

finding.summary: No upper bound on `dp` anywhere; an out-of-range decimal count makes `safeFormat` throw an uncaught `RangeError`, and the value is persisted to the shared document (render DoS reachable from an untrusted .xlsx)
finding.evidence:
`safeFormat` (format.ts:9-19) only guards against a bad *locale*: the `catch` re-invokes `value.toLocaleString('en-US', options)` with the SAME `options`, so an out-of-range `minimumFractionDigits`/`maximumFractionDigits` (valid range 0–100, 0–20 on older engines) throws a second, uncaught `RangeError` out of `formatValue`. `formatValue` is called on every display path (`Sheet.toDisplayString`, sheet.ts:967; the render helper at sheet.ts:4719) and neither is wrapped in a try/catch (only three `catch` sites exist in view/worksheet.ts, none around render), so the grid stops rendering.

Nothing clamps `dp` on the way in:
- Untrusted file input: `mapNumberFormat` derives `dp` straight from the attacker-supplied xlsx `formatCode` via `decimalPlaces` — `code.match(/\.(0+)/)` then `match[1].length` (packages/sheets/src/import/xlsx-styles.ts:178-181, used at :279, :282, :297) with no cap. A workbook containing `<numFmt formatCode="0.` + 200 zeros + `"/>` yields `{nf:'number', dp:200}`, which is written into the collaborative document and then crashes the render for the importer and every collaborator who opens the sheet — a persisted, remote-file-triggered availability failure.
- The code under review is the new owner of the step and clamps only the low side: `const clamped = stepped < 0; const target = clamped ? 0 : stepped;` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:4208-4209) — `changeDecimals(1)` increments without limit, so ~101 Increase clicks reach the same crash. The new pre-write check also evaluates `formatValue(value, nf, target, options)` (sheet.ts:4295) with that unbounded `target`, so the throw can now happen inside `changeDecimals` itself, before/instead of any write.
Fix directions: clamp `dp` where it is parsed and written (importer + `changeDecimals`), and/or make `safeFormat` fall back to an options-sanitised call rather than re-throwing.

verdict.reason: Every leg of the finding is contradicted by the working tree. (1) safeFormat does NOT re-throw: format.ts:40-60 has three fallback tiers, and the third (format.ts:56) calls value.toLocaleString('en-US') with NO options at all, explicitly commented "the options are the problem, not the locale", with String(value) as a final catch at :58. An out-of-range minimumFractionDigits therefore cannot escape formatValue; the options-sanitised fallback the reviewer prescribes as the fix already exists. The reviewer's cited range "format.ts:9-19" is the MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES doc comment, not safeFormat. (2) An upper bound on dp DOES exist: MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES = 20 (format.ts:14) applied by clampDecimals (format.ts:22-30) via Math.min(Math.max(Math.trunc(dp), 0), MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES), whose doc comment names the exact untrusted sources the finding cites (imported .xlsx, a collaborator's document). formatValue clamps on every numeric branch at format.ts:182 (consumed at :191-192, :207-208, :216-217) and renderedDecimals clamps at :160. So the untrusted-xlsx vector is neutralised: decimalPlaces (xlsx-styles.ts:178-181) is indeed uncapped and dp:200 can be stored, but it is clamped to 20 before reaching Intl, yielding a long-but-valid string rather than a RangeError - no render DoS, so the "no try/catch around render" observation is moot. (3) changeDecimals clamps the HIGH side two lines above the reviewer's quoted snippet: sheet.ts:4202 does Math.min(dp + delta, MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES) (imported at sheet.ts:63), so repeated Increase clicks saturate at 20 and the pre-write formatValue receives an already-bounded target. The headline claim "No upper bound on dp anywhere" is factually false.

finding.summary: `safeFormat`'s fallback re-throws for the same bad argument, so an untrusted `dp`/`cu` in stored style crashes every render (persistent client-side DoS)
finding.evidence: `safeFormat` (format.ts:14-18) catches a failure from `value.toLocaleString(locale, options)` and retries with `'en-US'` and the *same* `options`. The only errors Intl raises here are argument errors — `RangeError: minimumFractionDigits value is out of range` (dp > 20/100) and `RangeError: Invalid currency code` (a `cu` that is not a well-formed ISO code) — and neither is fixed by changing the locale, so the retry throws again and the RangeError escapes `formatValue`. `formatValue` is called unguarded in the render path (`packages/sheets/src/view/gridcanvas.ts:1596` with `style?.dp` and `currency: style?.cu`, no try/catch) and now also from the new `Sheet.unsetKeepsRendering` (`sheet.ts:4294-4295`, which passes `currency: effective?.cu` straight from stored cell style). Attack: a crafted .xlsx whose `numFmt` code has >20 decimal placeholders reaches `{ nf: 'number', dp: decimalPlaces(...) }` (`packages/sheets/src/import/xlsx-styles.ts:297`) with no upper bound, or a malicious collaborator writes `{nf:'currency', cu:'XX!'}`/`{dp: 300}` into the shared document; every client that renders that cell then throws inside the canvas draw loop and the sheet stops rendering for everyone, persistently, because the bad value is stored. Root cause is pre-existing (the diff relocates the write and adds one new call site), so treat it as a hardening gap this change inherits: `formatValue` should clamp `dp` and validate `cu` (or the fallback should drop the offending option) before handing them to Intl.

verdict.reason: The described code does not exist. The finding claims `safeFormat` retries only with the same `options` under a different locale and therefore re-throws the argument-level RangeError. The actual `safeFormat` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/format.ts:40-60) has a third fallback at :56 that calls `value.toLocaleString('en-US')` with NO options — dropping the offending `currency`/fraction-digit options — followed by a terminal `catch { return String(value); }` at :57-58. It cannot throw. An invalid `cu` like 'XX!' fails at :46 and :51 and then formats fine at :56. The unbounded-`dp` half is likewise not present: `formatValue` never hands raw `dp` to Intl; :182 computes `clampDecimals(dp, 2)` and only that clamped value reaches the option objects (:191-192, :207-208, :216-217). `clampDecimals` (:22-30) drops non-finite values and clamps to [0, MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES=20] (:14), so `dp: 300` or an xlsx numFmt with >20 placeholders yields 20, not a RangeError. The exact mitigations the finding recommends ("clamp dp and validate cu, or have the fallback drop the offending option") are already implemented; the lines it cites as the vulnerable `safeFormat` (14-18) are actually the MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES constant and clampDecimals doc comment. The cited call sites (gridcanvas.ts:1596, sheet.ts:972, 4309-4310, 4734) all route through `formatValue`, so no RangeError escapes into the paint path and the persistent-DoS chain cannot be completed. The only other raw Intl call (locale.ts:111-121, which does lack a third tier) is unreachable with untrusted input: its sole caller `buildLocaleFormatPreview` (:179-193) passes hardcoded 2-digit constants and a currency from the fixed CurrencyByRegion whitelist (:27-73), never cell style.
